#54157. How the Antigravity 360 Drone Will Change Your Travels

📅 23 Apr 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1547 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nomadicmatt ↗ Open Full Page

How the Antigravity 360 Drone Will Change Your Travels

📅 23 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1547 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • And, while there’s lots of restrictions around them, a lot of travelers take them on road because they produce some amazing sweeping aerial shots.
  • There’s lots of amazing brands out there but one that I think is super cool is the Antigravity A1.
  • I was sent one to use and want to share my experience and why I like this product so much.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Drones are huge. And, while there’s lots of restrictions around them, a lot of travelers take them on road because they produce some amazing sweeping aerial shots.

There’s lots of amazing brands out there but one that I think is super cool is the Antigravity A1. Released in late 2025, attempts to render the traditional gimbal obsolete for a vast segment of creators. By leveraging a dual-lens 360-degree capture system, the A1 records everything in every direction simultaneously. The result is a “fly now, frame later” experience that feels less like piloting a drone and more like directing a virtual camera in a pre-recorded digital environment.

I was sent one to use and want to share my experience and why I like this product so much.

Recent findings suggest that what make’s Antigravity 360’s so special is the two lenses. Most drones feature a single lens that points forward. However, the A1 features two ultra-wide-angle lenses positioned on the top and bottom of the central fuselage that each captures a 200-degree field of view. When those images are combines, they overlap to create a seamless 360-degree sphere.

And, in the final exported footage, the drone itself is digitally removed, creating the illusion of a camera floating in mid-air with no visible means of support.

Recent findings suggest that the sensors themselves are 1/1.28-inch CMOS units. While smaller than the 1-inch sensors found on some “Pro” level photography drones, they are massive compared to typical 360 action cameras. This allows for significantly better low-light performance and a higher dynamic range, capturing details in the highlights and shadows that would typically be lost in the harsh contrast of a midday sun.

It has been revealed that most countries require drones weighing 250 grams or more to be registered and subject to stricter flight rules. Antigravity clearly understood the importance of this threshold because they made the A1 to weigh exactly 249 grams with its standard battery meaning it’s not considered a commercial drone so you don’t have to register it.

And the drone feels remarkably sturdy. It utilizes a high-grade carbon-fiber-reinforced polymer that offers a better strength-to-weight ratio than the standard ABS plastic found in cheaper models. The folding mechanism is satisfyingly tactile, clicking into place with a precision that suggests long-term durability. When folded, the drone is roughly the size of a large smartphone, though about three times as thick.

It has been revealed that the Vision Goggles: These are sleek, lightweight, and feature dual 4K micro-OLED displays with a 120Hz refresh rate. The latency is nearly non-existent and they have integrated head tracking. Because the drone is recording in 360 degrees, you aren’t limited to seeing what is in front of the drone. When you turn your head to the left, the goggle feed pans to the left. If you look down, you see the ground passing beneath you. This provides a sense of presence and spatial awareness that is simply impossible with a traditional fixed-camera drone.

The drone uses a single-handed motion controller. You point the controller where you want to go and pull the trigger to accelerate. Tilt your wrist left to bank, or raise the nose of the controller to climb. It is an incredibly intuitive system that allows even a novice to fly through complex environments within minutes. For professional FPV pilots who prefer the precision of manual acrobatic flight, the A1 does support a traditional “Mode 2” stick controller, but the motion controls are so fluid that most consumers will likely never switch back.

Here’s a video of the drone in action:.

The marketing for the Antigravity 360 proudly displays “8K Resolution.” In a traditional camera, 8K means every pixel is packed into a 16:9 rectangle. In 360 video, those pixels are spread across a full sphere. When you “reframe” that 8K sphere into a standard flat video, you are looking at a “crop” of the total image.

The color science is noticeably improved over previous 360 cameras. The A1 features a “Vivid” profile for those who want punchy, social-media-ready colors, and a 10-bit “Log” profile for professional editors who need to match the footage to other cameras in a color-grading suite. The stabilization, powered by Antigravity’s “FlowState” algorithms, is nothing short of miraculous. You can fly in 20mph winds, and the footage remains as steady as if the camera were on a tripod.

The “Antigravity Studio” app allows you to download footage wirelessly (at speeds up to 80MB/s) and reframe your video using your phone’s gyroscope. You simply watch the video and move your phone around to “film” the scene in real-time. The app also features “Auto-Frame,” an AI tool that identifies subjects and automatically generates a cut that keeps them in focus. For a solo creator, this effectively provides a virtual camera crew that never misses a shot.

Sources indicate that battery technology remains the bottleneck for all small drones. The A1’s standard Intelligent Flight Battery provides a theoretical 24 minutes of flight. In real-world conditions with moderate wind and constant recording, expect closer to 19 or 20 minutes.

Sources indicate that while 20 minutes sounds short, the “work per minute” is much higher than a traditional drone. Because you don’t need to re-fly a path to get different angles, a single 20-minute flight can yield the same amount of usable footage as three flights with a Mavic. For those who need more time, the “Pro Battery” (which pushes the weight over 250g) offers a staggering 39 minutes of flight time, though it does compromise the drone’s agility slightly.

In terms of flight dynamics, the A1 is a “cinewhoop” style flyer. It is stable and predictable rather than aggressive and twitchy. It has a top speed of roughly 36 mph, which is plenty for following bikes or cars, but it won’t keep up with a professional racing drone. The “Turtle Mode” is a life-saver; if you crash and end up upside down, the drone can flip itself over using its propellers, allowing you to take off again without a “walk of shame” to recover the aircraft.

The Antigravity 360 is a niche product that is rapidly becoming mainstream.

It has been revealed that the Antigravity 360 (A1) is the most exciting drone I have tested. By removing the need for a gimbal and the stress of manual framing, it allows the pilot to focus on the one thing that truly matters: the story they are trying to tell.

Sources indicate that while the image quality isn’t quite at the level of a high-end cinema drone, and the lenses are admittedly delicate, these are small prices to pay for the creative liberation the A1 provides. It bridges the gap between traditional cinematography and the immersive world of VR.

If you are a creator who is tired of the same old “drone shots” and want to push the boundaries of what is possible in the air, the Antigravity 360 is an essential addition to your toolkit.

Outsite Review: The Best Place to Stay for Digital Nomads

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that balancing travel and remote work will always be one of the biggest challenges on the road. When you’re a digital nomad, it’s always a struggle to balance sightseeing and also get your work done in a nice, quiet environment. No one wants to spend hours searching for a coffee shop or be in one that is uncomfortable. It is something I’ve struggled with a lot in the past.

Working from the road used to mean hunching over a tiny hostel common room table or arguing with an Airbnb host who swore their internet was “super fast” (only to find out it couldn’t even load a basic email).

But, as remote work has expanded post-pandemic, a ton of coliving spaces have popped up that combine the benefits of a coworking space with the social atmosphere of a hostel (but without the dorm-style basic amenities). They are meant for those digital nomads who want a nice place to stay where they can not only get work done but also meet other travelers (as remote work can be isolating since you’re doing it alone)!

The biggest and most popular platform for remote workers doing this is Outsite, which has a lot of beautiful locations around the world.

And, in this post, I’ll go over everything you need to know about them and my experience staying with them on a recent trip to Bordeaux.

Founded in 2015, Outsite is a global network of coliving and coworking spaces designed specifically for remote workers, location-independent entrepreneurs, and digital nomads.

They started with a single house in Santa Cruz, California, aimed at people who wanted to surf and work. Today, they have over 5,000 members and 50 locations you can choose from.

Industry observers note that currently, anyone can book a stay at Outsite but if you’re a member, you get access to more perks and better rates. You can pay a yearly membership of $199 or pay once for a lifetime membership at $499. Perks include access to members-only locations, 1 week free in newly introduced destinations, 50% off in flash sales, 40% off extended stays, new member mixers, a job & sublets board, and some lifestyle perks.

It’s easy to use, too. You just browse their website, filter by destination or the type of vibe you want (beach, city, mountains), and book your private room.

According to recent reports, outsite operates like a boutique hotel meets a coworking space. When you book an Outsite, you are booking a private bedroom. Most rooms have their own private en-suite bathrooms, though some budget-friendly rooms share a bathroom with one other person.

According to recent reports, every location features massive, beautifully furnished communal areas. You get to enjoy fully-equipped chef’s kitchens that you could never afford in a solo Airbnb. Plus, you get spacious living rooms, outdoor patios, and often roof decks or pools (location depending).

It has been revealed that every single location has a dedicated coworking space built right into the house. I’m talking ergonomic chairs, plenty of outlets, monitors you can plug into, and blazing-fast, enterprise-grade Wi-Fi. You can wake up, make your coffee, and be at a proper desk in a state of deep focus within five minutes.

Plus, there’s a social aspect to all Outside locations. Every location has a dedicated Community Manager. Before you even arrive, you are added to a local WhatsApp group and locations organize weekly events like family-style dinners, group weekend trips, Friday night tapas crawls, and morning yoga sessions. You really get a lot of chances to meet people.

According to recent reports, and the community manager is a great resource. During my stay at their Bordeaux location, they were available to share tips, suggest places to eat, and just be there to answer any questions I had. It was really helpful.

Industry observers note that first, the properties are really nice. Their place in Bordeaux had modern furniture, comfy chairs to work from, laundry facilities, and even a small gym. The rooms were really nice too. I had a private desk, a comfy bed, and a really lovely bathroom (the water had GREAT shower pressure!).

Recent findings suggest that the shared kitchen was super clean (cleaners come daily) and the counter space was huge. It was the kind of kitchen I wish my house had. You could cook some really good meals here. (Coffee and tea are always provided for free!).

Recent findings suggest that plus, I love the design. The spaces are designed with natural light, plants, and local art. It feels incredibly far removed from the sterile environment of a corporate hotel. It feels like you are staying at your very wealthy, very cool friend’s house.

According to recent reports, however, for me, the main draw for using Outsite is the community aspect. Being a remote worker means you’re often working alone. Whether in a hotel or a coffee shop, it’s just you and your community. It’s hard to meet people.

According to recent reports, at Outsite, you are surrounded by your fellow digital nomads who can relate to your life experience. They aren’t backpackers on a trip wondering why you are sitting on your computer all day when you should be exploring. Because everyone is there to work and live, there’s a shared bond. You’re there to work and have fun. Most people at the Bordeaux location were there for at least two weeks. Our community manager organized a bunch of weekend events to help people get to know each other, too.

First, Outsite is not a budget backpacker option. If you are used to spending $15 a night in a dorm room in Southeast Asia, Outsite is not for you. You are paying a premium for the private room, the guaranteed workspace, and the community curation. That mentioned, when you factor in the cost of renting an Airbnb plus buying a monthly pass to a local coworking space, Outsite likely comes out cheaper.

Recent findings suggest that second, the popular locations book up fast. If you want to spend July in their Lisbon house or January in their Costa Rica location, you need to book months in advance. You can’t always be spontaneous with their most sought-after properties.

Recent findings suggest that do I have to be a member to book a stay? No! Anyone can book a stay at Outsite. However, if you strategy on staying for more than a few days, the $199 annual Membership pays for itself almost immediately through the discounted nightly rates.

It has been revealed that is there an age limit? There is no official age limit, but you must be at least 18 (and in some locations, 21) to book. The vast majority of guests are working professionals in their late 20s, 30s, and 40s. It definitely skews a bit older and more professional than your average backpacker hostel.

It has been revealed that is there a minimum number of nights required? For most locations, the minimum stay is just 2 nights, making it easy to pop in for a weekend. However, some specific locations (especially in major cities with strict local housing laws like Fresh York) may require a 30-day minimum stay.

Sources indicate that can I bring my pet? Generally, no. Because it is a shared living environment with communal kitchens and living spaces, most Outsite locations do not allow pets to ensure the comfort of all guests (and to prevent allergy complications).

Living the digital nomad life shouldn’t mean sacrificing your career progression, your comfort, or your social life. You shouldn’t have to choose between traveling the world and having a comfortable desk chair, or seeing newly introduced cities and having a consistent group of friends. I met some cool people while I stayed with them in Bordeaux.

In a recent development, outsite is a great platform for people who want the perks and comforts of a private home, the productivity of an office, and the social life of a hostel. I think sharing a home creates a sense of intimacy, and you will absolutely make some friends out of it.

Be sure to check them out on your next trip and go find your tribe!

No more permanent coalitions: What the midterm results reveal

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, senate Democratic leader Charles E.
  • ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once said.
  • In a recent development, in 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, senate Democratic leader Charles E. Schumer poses in his office on Nov. 9 for a group photo with incoming members of his caucus: from left, Ohio's Sherrod Brown, Texas' James Talarico, Iowa's Josh Turek, Michigan's Abdul El-Sayed, North Carolina's Roy Cooper, Illinois' Juliana Stratton, Latest Hampshire's Chris Pappas, South Carolina's Annie Andrews, Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan, Maine's Troy Jackson and Kansas' Adam Hamilton. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once said. “If you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.”.

In a recent development, in 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness. Republicans had captured the White House, flipped the Senate and held the House. President Donald Trump had completely altered the party coalitions as he led the ascendant GOP to victory.

According to recent reports, now, just two years later, Democrats are on the rise. A historic midterm tsunami has swept them into such commanding Senate and House majorities that some are questioning whether Republicans will ever be in charge again. And if Texas is blue, how does the GOP have any chance in the Electoral College again?

A big takeaway from the midterm results should be that there’s very little permanence in our politics.

What may have looked like a upcoming GOP coalition was really more of a Trump coalition, and it crumbled in the face of economic frustrations, affordability concerns and the president’s unpopular policies.

With Trump’s negative job approval rating weighing them down, Republican candidates suffered losses among virtually all demographic groups – including by wide margins among constituencies thought to make up the GOP’s core.

Trump or the Republicans finished ahead among male voters by 4 points in 2018, 8 points in 2020, 14 points in 2022 and 12 points in 2024, according to the exit polls. Men went for Democratic candidates by 4 points (51 percent to 47 percent) this cycle. Meanwhile, Republicans lost even more ground among women. While Kamala Harris finished ahead of Trump by 8 points in 2024, that margin grew to 21 points for Democratic candidates this year.

Trump closed the gap among Hispanic voters to just 5 points behind Harris two years ago. This year, Hispanic voters nationwide supported Democratic candidates by 32 points (65 percent to 33 percent). Even white voters shifted significantly. They backed Trump or  Republican candidates by 10 points in 2018, 17 points in 2020, 18 points in 2022 and 15 points in 2024. And yet Democrats edged out Republicans by a point (50 percent to 49 percent) on Nov. 3.

Industry observers note that voters without a college degree were supposed to be a key cog in Republicans’ newly introduced populist coalition. But they went from +13 (56 percent to 43 percent) for Trump in 2024 to backing Republican candidates by just 1 point this year. Meanwhile, the gap among voters with a college degree went from 14 points for Harris in 2024 to 30 points for Democrats this cycle.

Republicans had closed the gap among young voters aged 18 to 29 from 35 points in 2018 to just 11 points in 2024. But younger voters supported Democratic candidates this year by 50 points (74 percent to 24 percent). Not to mention Democrats flipped voters aged 45 to 64 for the first time in nearly two decades.

In a recent development, white evangelicals appear to be one of the only groups that didn’t shift toward Democrats. They supported GOP candidates 82 percent to 17 percent. But they only made up 17 percent of the electorate, according to the exit polls, which is down from a very consistent 25 percent for more than a decade. So there was still a problem with that group of voters, but it was more about turnout than persuasion.

Sources indicate that while there was an unmistakable leftward shift this year, the results should not be considered a permanent party realignment any more than 2024 was. While Democrats did extremely well in Texas this year, they still haven’t won the Lone Star State in a presidential race in 50 years. So maybe it’s wise for everyone to take a deep breath.

According to recent reports, if you take this year’s election results and match them with the Senate seats on the ballot in 2028, there doesn’t appear to be a viable path for Republicans back to the majority. But there wasn’t a particularly viable Democratic path to the Senate majority at this point two years ago. And if the Alaska election goes their way, they will end up winning Senate races in seven states that were initially rated Solid Republican.

In a recent development, if one party starts to get too comfortable, voters have a way of bringing politicians back down to earth. If Democrats come to Congress and push too far to the left or become too defined by their most extreme members, they will squander the opportunity they earned this year.

The dramatic demographic swings should be evidence that many voters are not beholden to either party and are open to switching allegiances, particularly in a time of economic uncertainty.

At the same time, if Republicans don’t go through some time of reflection and instead triple down on the policies that led to the blue wave, they risk cementing some of the shifts that started this cycle. It just won’t be thick cement.

Intervine has added Susurrus Sparkling Teas to its portfolio, expanding its premium non-alcoholic offerings for onboard programs.

According to a press release, Susurrus brings a fine-wine perspective to organic sparkling tea, with an emphasis on origin, vintage and terroir, resulting in a premium experience with the same sophistication as wine.

It has been revealed that “The world of tea is just as vast and fascinating as the world of wine. Sparkling tea is its own newly introduced, distinct category that can bring the best of these two worlds together,” said Ellison Wofford, founder of Susurrus Sparkling Teas.

It has been revealed that “I crafted Susurrus to be appealing to a broad audience because you can enjoy it for what it is—single-origin, single-cultivar, organic tea—rather than for what it lacks: alcohol. I am beyond thrilled to partner with Intervine. Together, we will provide a healthy, refreshing, and elegant option to guests of all kinds while traveling.”.

Unlike dealcoholized wine, Susurrus is inherently non-alcoholic, with tea leaves cold-steeped instead fermented, and the finished teas carbonated at pressure levels comparable to Champagne and sparkling wine.

There are at the moment two varieties: Magnolia Oolong and Osmanthus Golden Tip, both of which come from hand-harvested teas that Wofford directly imports from China.

Designed to be served chilled in a flute or white wine glass, the teas offer their own distinctive flavor profiles and are designed to complement food, providing an alternative to wine.

“I was blown away the first time I tasted Ellison’s lovely creations,” noted Jonjie Lockman, CEO of Intervine.

“‘Champagne’s sober sister,’ as we like to refer to it, provides sophistication, depth of flavors, and complexity in abundance. The Intervine team is proud to bring this special beverage to our airline, airport, and cruise line customers from across the world.”.

It has been revealed that the annual fee for the card is just $95, which means it’s effectively free once you factor in the two statement credits. In a recent development, both options are super easy to implement, which is why this is a great card for newbies. And if this is the only way that you’ll use your miles, go for it! Using them is better than letting them sit around.

However, you can usually get more for your miles when you transfer them to Capital One’s transfer partners.

The ability to transfer to travel partners is what makes Capital One miles valuable. While the actual value varies based on what you book, you can usually find airline and hotel redemptions worth much more than the aforementioned 1 cent per mile.

Transferring to travel partners is a bit more work than using the portal, but there are more tools than ever to help you maximize your miles (such as point.me for finding flights and Awayz for finding award hotel stays).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

My favorite thing about San Juan? You can have a morning that feels plucked out of a history book, an afternoon that commits you entirely to the beach, and a night that’s topped off with a frosty Medalla, sweet rum cocktail, and flirty bachata dance. It’s glitzy yet lush, historic yet ever-evolving, a city delightfully full of contrasts, and one I will never run out of reasons to revisit.

Recent findings suggest that my father’s side of the family is from Puerto Rico, so I’ve been coming back to the island for years, and I love that there’s always another corner to get to know. There’s Old San Juan, with all its pastel-painted façades, galleries and shops, blue cobblestone streets, and tucked-away restaurants; Condado and Ocean Park for long, sea-salty afternoons by the ocean; and Santurce, where street murals, galleries, haute dining, and a lively bar scene bring a fresh, creative vibe to the city.

It has been revealed that of course, there’s no shortage of hotels in San Juan, but sometimes a vacation to the island’s capital calls for a little more room to sprawl, or a front door that opens onto a lush little neighborhood rather than a buzzy hotel lobby. The city’s best Airbnbs offer just that, along with wonderful amenities, whether it’s a private pool hidden behind swaying palms or a breezy courtyard for sipping on some local morning coffee.

Consider this your invitation to soak up the sun in Puerto Rico's capital for a few days. Read on for nine of the best Airbnbs in San Juan to consider for your next trip.

We've selected these listings based on Superhost status, ratings, amenities, location, decor, editor stays, and previous guest reviews.

Number of guests: 5Bed and bath: 2 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Unique design, proximity to the beach, city skyline views, fully equipped kitchen.

Seemingly an ode to the vibrant murals and culture found in Santurce, to describe this Airbnb as “colorful” is simply an understatement. You’ll never be bored at this retro-inspired haven, what with its groovy wallpaper in nearly every room, playful lava lamps, disco ball, and hanging plants. Conveniently, it's situated right in the heart of San Juan’s food and arts district and just a few steps from Ocean Park Beach. If you do decide to stay in for the night, rinse off the sand in your designer rain shower, throw a vinyl on the record player, and cook up some local produce in the fully stocked kitchen. Thanks to the in-unit washer and dryer, you’ll likely depart with no dirty beach laundry. As for the sleeping arrangements? The space can fit up to five guests, but there’s only two bedrooms. So if you’re doubling up, the fifth guest would have to crash on the living room’s sofa bed.

Neighborhood: SanturceThings to do nearby: Ocean Park, Calle Loiza, Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico.

Number of guests: 6Bed and bath: 3 bedrooms, 1 bathWhy we love it: Private pool and patio, central location, fully equipped kitchen, in-unit washer and dryer.

A group-friendly villa that’s close to Old San Juan, buzzy beaches, and its very own private pool? Sign me up. This central Carolina base is for those seeking out an easy, breezy group trip, whether traveling with friends or family. The interiors are all very simple, with neutral colors and subtle art pieces hanging above the bar area and around the airy living room. The bedrooms have just what you need to feel at home; two offer a queen bed, and the third fits in two singles. Perhaps the biggest perk of all: The back of the house is lined with floor-to-ceiling glass doors, which open out to the small-but-mighty backyard, where a plunge pool that doubles as an outdoor bar will tempt you to stay a while.

Neighborhood: CarolinaThings to do nearby: Isla Verde Beach, Hacienda Campo Rico, Placita de Santurce, Old San Juan, La Factoria.

After a day of venturing to the capital city, its thoughtful touches make relaxing in style that much easier: Cool off in the outdoor shower, escape the island heat in the AC, or sway in the hammock with a good book. When it’s time to unwind, cue up a film on the living room's projector, or head to either of the two bedrooms, where queen beds and smart TVs await.

Recent findings suggest that tucked into a quieter pocket of Hato Rey—the city's urban hub known as Milla de Oro, or “the Golden Mile”—this home keeps you away from the chaos of crowded sidewalks yet right in the middle of the best restaurants, nightlife, and venues. You’ll also be just a short drive away from some of the city’s most beloved beaches, from Condado Beach to Capitol and beyond.

Neighborhood: Hato ReyThings to do nearby: Plaza Las Americas, Hiram Bithorn Stadium, Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot ("El Choli"), La Santa Rooftop and Cocktail Bar.

Each of the bedrooms is roomy, and you’ll find a separate dining area for meals at home, a bright and airy living room to talk about all your adventures from the day, and a sleek kitchen with deep green cabinets. Outside, hang out on the backyard patio to read or listen to music in the hammock surrounded by swaying palms, and take in this midcentury-modern home—there aren’t many like this in the capital with this much space and access to the finer things of the city. (Yes, mentioned finer things do include heading to La Placita to get your bachata on.).

Neighborhood: CarolinaThings to do nearby: Isla Verde Beach, Carolina Public Beach, Old San Juan, Hacienda Campo Rico, La Placita.

Equal parts convenient and stylish, this tastefully restored 1962 home offers a surprising amount of open space given its hyper-central city location. Inside, you’ll find light-filled living and dining areas that flow into three roomy bedrooms decked out in colorful walls, over-the-bed tapestries, and lush greenery. The hosts note they drew design inspiration from the “serene and vibrant colors of the city’s golden hour and sunsets”—views you and your crew can soak in from a rooftop bar in Old San Juan, a 15-minute drive away, on Isla Verde Beach 10 minutes away, or poolside in your very own backyard.

Neighborhood: Hato ReyThings to do nearby: Plaza Las Americas, Hiram Bithorn Stadium, Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot ("El Choli"), Casita Hato Rey, Castillo San Cristóbal.

Recent findings suggest that positioned in the heart of the city’s bustling Calle Loíza—lined with shops, restaurants, bars, and nightlife—this cozy abode grants the access and amenities needed for an effortless stay in San Juan. Fire up a coffee in the full kitchenette and enjoy it on the patio hammock, where there’s also a soaking tub and two robes for some breezy post-beach rejuvenation. This lofty apartment sits on the third floor (accessible only via stairs) and is ideal for a duo given its one-bedroom setup. (The listing can technically sleep up to four with a queen-size sofa bed, just in case you want to extend the invite.).

Sources indicate that talk about vintage galore! This bold, retro-inspired stay is the perfect mix of quirky and tasteful. You’ll likely leave feeling inspired by the intention and design from the host of this one-bedroom apartment. But try to commit to the bit and fall into the old-school sentiment with a more analog stay. Meaning? Quit the scrolling. Instead, play some tunes on the record player, dance under the disco ball, unwind on the front porch’s swing chair, and jump right into the comfy, ergonomic mattress. When it’s time to head out, you’re in walking distance of the beach and a quick drive to the sweet cobblestone streets of Old San Juan.

Neighborhood: SanturceThings to do nearby: Ocean Park Beach, Calle Loíza, Las Marias, Playa del Pueblo, Old San Juan.

Number of guests: 3Bed and bath: 1 bedroom, 1 bathWhy we love it: Rain shower, private patio, indoor hammock, design-forward, walkable to beach.

It has been revealed that in the mood for some island romance? There’s no better place for love than this gorgeous apartment with the sea in easy reach. With interiors curated by Dreamers Welcome, a Puerto Rico–based hospitality group focused on luxury stays with a laid-back vibe, you’ll also have exclusive access to amenities at nearby boutique hotel Dreamcatcher by DW. This includes a daily vegan or vegetarian breakfast, guided tours, yoga on the beach, and a gift store to shop at with crafts by local creatives. Back at the apartment, take in the views from the intimate patio space, sway on the indoor hammock, and fall into the ever-cozy sofa. With a double vanity and rich red polished shower, even a trip to the bathroom here will make you feel like you’re in a design magazine.

Neighborhood: SanturceThings to do nearby: Condado, Ocean Park, Old San Juan, Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico, Miramar.

Number of guests: 8Bed and bath: 4 bedrooms, 3 bathsWhy we love it: Private pool, barbecue, outdoor seating area, beach access, kid-friendly amenities.

This sunny gem of an Airbnb makes group getaways look easy. Just steps from the Ocean Park beach—where you’re sure to see kitesurfers aplenty—you’ll also have a pool to lounge in and around right at home. In fact, the backyard is bigger than it first appears: There’s a separate barbecue area, as well as a swing chair and a canopy day bed for the best kind of outdoor nap. Located in a gated community, you’ll have privacy as well as peace and quiet, but not without easy access to the local hot spots that make San Juan the buzzy city that it is.

Industry observers note that each of the bedrooms has sweet design touches, from whimsy and bright colors to room-darkening shades and comfy linens. The fourth bedroom is located in a separate, more private space with its own bathroom, so it’s best for those who value more privacy, or the parents on a family vacation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Gemini, a 960-passenger ship formerly operated by Miray Cruises, was reportedly sold in an auction held by Greek authorities on November 18, 2026.

According to financial and business news portal Fresh Money, the ship, which was auctioned to settle debts of its former operator and owner, was acquired by an undisclosed buyer.

The 3,806,562.75 euro paid is slightly higher than the auction’s opening bid, which was set at Gemini’s project scrap value of 3,805,462 euros.

Fresh Money noted that four companies expressed interest in acquiring the 19,093-ton vessel that was originally built in 1992 for Crown Cruise Line.

As previously reported by Cruise Industry News, the auction was originally scheduled to take place in late October but was later postponed due to an objection filed by DenizBank with the Single-Member Court of First Instance of Piraeus.

The Turkish bank opposed the initial auction, claiming that the vessel is worth more than its scrap value thanks to 2025 repairs and asking the authorities to increase the opening bid price to 14 million euros.

Greek authorities seized the ship in Karystos earlier this year over a monetary claim of approximately 22,772 euros, followed by its towing to the Port of Elefsis, near Piraeus, in late June, where it remains docked.

The Gemini was last in service in 2025, offering a series of short cruises to Turkey and the Greek Islands.

It was scheduled to operate a cruise program in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Black Sea this summer, but the deployment was cancelled due to Miray’s financial concerns.

Industry observers note that rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.

Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.

“This is so nervewracking,” she mentioned, before pulling out a chip with a “1” printed on it.

According to recent reports, her prize was a coveted one — first choice of office space. Every two years, incoming members of the House play a game of chance to see who can land the best real estate and who will be relegated to less desirable corners of the Capitol complex.

According to recent reports, the room broke out in raucous applause and a standing ovation. Her new colleagues started singing “Happy Birthday.”.

In a recent development, not everyone was so lucky. Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira, R-Texas, pulled number 105 — the very last one. The former MLB player raised his arms in a mock celebration.

“Lets all hope for the luck of the Taylors,” remarked Rep.-elect Brent Taylor, R-Tenn., only to emerge with number 81.

The newly-elected members got their turn in a random order, walking up one by one to a table where deputy executive director of House Office Buildings Kornell Rancy kept watch over the box of chips.

According to recent reports, rep.-elect John Cowan, R-Ga., was the first to pick a number. The first neurosurgeon to be elected to Congress, Cowan wore his white doctor’s coat as he pulled number 11 out of the box.

“I wanted to do something where I’m just representing health care providers around the country,” Cowan remarked.

As returning members lay claim to more desirable offices made available by those who resign, retire or lose elections, the space they’ve abandoned is left for the newcomers, who are on the Hill this week for orientation. Many of them will end up in the Longworth Building, where suites can be awkward or cramped.

In a recent development, not all offices are created equal, and the calculus has changed over the years. The previously undesirable Cannon Building just underwent a budget-busting renovation that lasted more than a decade, with a spacious courtyard opening earlier this year. But the coveted Rayburn Building still retains its prestige, despite repeated and dire warnings from the Architect of the Capitol about its crumbling infrastructure.

“You’re welcome,” said Rep.-elect Amish Shah, D-Ariz., after pulling a disappointing number 94.

Prior to the lottery, Rep.-elect Trever Nehls, R-Texas, was hoping for the best but had a backup initiative in case his number said otherwise.

Industry observers note that “If I don’t pick number one, I’m going to offer one of these cigars as a trade to whoever gets it,” he said, pointing to three of them sticking out of his jacket pocket. He’s preparing to take over the seat presently held by his twin brother Troy, who shares a fondness for stogies.

The office space lottery dates back to 1908, when members of the 60th Congress received their first office assignments after the completion of what would be named the Cannon Building. A House page drew names and numbers from a box, and members selected their offices from a chart, according to House Office Buildings executive director of facility operations Joe Yates, who kicked things off Tuesday with a history lesson.

The lottery now is a little more modern, with members poring over virtual office layouts and doing walkthroughs of spaces on laptops.

“If somebody had to get 105, I’m glad it was me because I am here to serve, and I’m serving my freshman class by picking the worst office,” Teixeira said. “This is low on my priority list.”.

Some members revealed their lucky draws themselves, while others let Yates break the news.

“Come visit me,” noted Rep.-elect Chris Gober, R-Texas, after pulling number 2 from the box.

After the lottery itself, members huddled with their staff to strategize about the next steps — how to leverage their numbers and select the best suites left on the list, while also exploring layouts, paint colors and carpeting.

“First and foremost, a good layout, so we can do good work, and people can be comfortable in doing the work, and then a convenient location. Very utilitarian,” said Rep.-elect Scott Wiener, D-Calif., of his priorities.

“We’ll get a decent Longworth office,” said Wiener, who drew pick 43. “Cannon would have been ideal, but I’m happy with any office.”.

Rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, D-Colo., was hoping to replicate the good luck of some of his colleagues. “I’m going to do the Shannon Taylor and Sam Forstag. It’s eyes closed, behind the back,” he stated of his moves, reaching into the box. But it wasn’t enough, and Rutinel pulled number 69.

In a recent development, “These are not red numbers, these are not blue numbers. These are the remaining numbers, and there ain’t that many,” noted Rep.-elect Johnny Garcia, D-Texas, who was among the last few people to pick. He emerged with number 75.

And when Rep.-elect Joe Strada, R-Fla., the last of the incoming members to draw, walked up to the table, the whole room cheered.

“Wouldn’t it be crazy if I picked number 1?” he joked, pulling out the last chip in the box.

I grew up just outside of Toronto and went to university in Montreal, so needless to say, I know cold. I’m no stranger to below-zero temperatures, snow up to my shins, and slippery strolls to and from extra-curricular activities. And if there’s one brand we trust to keep us warm—and keep us moving—up in Canada, it’s The North Face.

According to recent reports, I’ve been donning The North Face’s parkas, snow boots, and insulating layers to stay toasty for as long as I can remember, but I’ve also brought the brand with me throughout my many travels. I still think fondly of the turquoise backpack-duffel combo that I took across Europe when I studied abroad in 2016, and in recent years, I’ve taken to the website to search for fanny packs, hiking boots, rain jackets, and other accessories for outdoor adventures (as well as to peruse the North Face x Skims outerwear collab, because I just can’t help myself). Plus, the quality is just unmatched, so I know I’ll have all of my gear for years to come.

Of course, between flights, hotels, and all the activities in between, travel can be expensive, so if you’re looking to save on gear, you’ve come to the right place. Read on for easy ways to get discounts on popular items from The North Face, including promo codes, sale picks, coupons, and more. Even better, we’re sharing some of our editors’ top recommendations from The North Face that you can save significant on now.

It has been revealed that if you haven’t yet joined The North Face’s loyalty program, XPLR Pass, now's the time. You'll earn 1 point for every $1 spent—and you can redeem $10 after gaining 100 points. Sources indicate that whether you’re about to head out on an all-weather adventure, are looking for something comfy to wear on your next staycation, or are prepping ahead for next winter, chances are you could benefit from a scroll through The North Face’s Black Friday sale section where you'll find up to 40% off some of the brand’s bestsellers. Some highlights? Save 30% off the women's Frost Fall hooded jacket, 30% off the Cragmont fleece jacket, and 40% off the men's Summit Series half-zip. Browse the sale section to find even more deals on winter jackets, zip-ups, vests, and more.

It has been revealed that in addition to the 10% off promo code at sign-up, XPLR Pass members get perks like free shipping on every order, access to exclusive products, a birthday treat, and points on all purchases. You earn 1 point for every $1 spent, and can trade in 100 points for a $10 reward, up to $50 off per cycle (rewards are converted into coupon codes in March, June, and October). But you don’t need to shop to earn points; you can also accrue them by bringing a reusable bag when you make an in-store purchase, sending a personal referral link to invite friends, using the app to check in at a The North Face store or a US National Park, and more.

The North Face rewards deserving individuals in demanding careers with 10% off products in-store and online. If you’re a student, teacher (including professors, faculty, and staff members), or military member, verify your status on the website using SheerID to receive your discount code.

The North Face takes sustainability seriously, and its Renewed and Remade programs allow customers to participate in the action. The North Face then takes your pre-loved items, cleans them, tunes them up, and sells them in its online Renewed store, where you can score gear for up to $250 off.

It has been revealed that the brand’s Remade program goes one step further, taking items that cannot be refurbished and upcycling them into one-of-a-kind pieces that are then sold at a major discount on the website. Unique gear that’s mindful of Mother Nature? Yes, please.

Madrid 5-Day Itinerary: A Guide to Culture, Gastronomy, and Local Life

📅 06 May 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2459 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nomadicmatt

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home to some 3.5 million people, Madrid is the capital of Spain and the country’s largest city.
  • Sources indicate that like Barcelona, Madrid is a city that starts late and goes slow.
  • Industry observers note that I love all my visits to Madrid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Home to some 3.5 million people, Madrid is the capital of Spain and the country’s largest city. Though it’s somewhat sprawling, the city boasts stunning architecture, incredible food, and an energetic nightlife that stretches until dawn. Over 10 million people visit the city each year, and the minute you step out to explore, you’ll understand why Madrid is one of Europe’s top destinations.

Sources indicate that like Barcelona, Madrid is a city that starts late and goes slow. It’s a city for night owls, where dinner starts late and the parties even later. But if you can embrace the laid-back pace of life, the slow meals, and the late-night vibes, you’ll have a more authentic visit and uncover the true beating heart of the city’s culture.

Industry observers note that I love all my visits to Madrid. I’ve been a few times over the years and the city never ceases to amaze me. The food, the energy, the art (so much art!). Madrid is just cool.

Being such a significant city, I know it can be easy to feel lost. Where do you start with what you want to do? Where do you go? It took me a few visits to figure it out.

In this post, I’ll help you blueprint an epic five-day visit to Madrid that will ensure you not only see the main sights but that you also get off the beaten path and see just what makes Madrid so popular — and all without breaking the bank either!

It has been revealed that this first day focuses on a prestigious area designated as a UNESCO World Heritage site in 2021. There are over 40 monuments and over 40 buildings on the site. It’s easily one of the most picturesque and historic areas of the city.

The route begins at the Prado Museum, one of the best museums on the planet. Here you’ll find works from El Greco, Velázquez, and Goya, as well as many other masters (such as Rubens, Botticelli, and Caravaggio to name a few). If you only visit one museum in Madrid, this is the one. It’s incredible and worth taking the time to explore. It’s one of the biggest museums in the world, too. Make sure you spend a few hours here at a minimum.

Just a 10-minute walk along the Paseo del Prado, the journey continues at the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, a private collection spanning from the Renaissance to Pop Art, and culminates at the Reina Sofía Museum. The Reina Sofía National Art Center offers a fantastic collection of modern art. Works by masters like Picasso, Miró, Kandinsky, Dalí, and Bacon can all be found here. The centerpiece is Picasso’s famous Guernica, a 1937 oil painting considered the most moving anti-war painting in the world. While I don’t love modern art, even I enjoyed this museum.

After museum hopping, it’s time to dive into Madrid’s culinary scene. Try Taberna La Fragua de Vulcano for a rustic atmosphere perfect for sampling cocido madrileño. If you are near the Reina Sofía Museum, don’t miss the vibrant garden terrace at Arzábal, renowned for having some of the best croquetas in the city. Finally, for a unique setting, Bodega de los Secretos lets you dine in restored 17th-century wine caves, making it the most atmospheric choice near the Prado Museum.

After a late lunch, spend some time exploring Madrid’s unique ‘House Museums. These are former private palaces that preserve the intimate atmosphere of their original owners. The crown jewel of this collection is the Sorolla Museum, the sun-drenched former residence of ‘the painter of light.’ Following a major architectural renovation, this underrated museum is set to reopen its doors in 2026, offering a refreshed look at its stunning gardens and Mediterranean canvases.

Or if you want something else, there is also the nearby Museum of Romanticism, where you can enjoy a coffee in its secret garden, or visit the Lázaro Galdiano Museum to marvel at a private collection of Goya, Murillo, Velázquez, El Greco, or Bosch housed in a magnificent neo-Renaissance mansion.

In the evening, enjoy some food and relaxation.

In a recent development, the second day delves into the medieval and Renaissance layout of the city, famously known as Habsburg Madrid (Madrid de los Austrias). The central hub is Puerta del Sol, where a photo at Kilometer Zero and the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue are mandatory for a traveler’s geographic check-in. Kilometer Zero is the official starting point of all the highways and railways in the country, making this effectively the center of the entire country. There’s a small plaque you can snap a photo of.

Recent findings suggest that nearby is the Bear and the Strawberry Tree statue (El Oso y el Madroño). The statue shows a bear reaching up to eat fruit from a madroño tree, symbols which come from Madrid’s coat of arms (the bear represents the city and the tree represents the land and nature surrounding it that has helped make it prosper).

Recent findings suggest that from here, walk toward the iconic Plaza Mayor, highlighting its porticoed architecture and the Casa de la Panadería. Plaza Mayor once hosted bullfights, markets, symphonies, tournaments, and even executions. Now it’s ringed with tourist shops, cafés, and restaurants. It’s a good place from which to indulge in some people-watching, offers some good (though overpriced) bars, and occasionally has concerts and events.

For a true “Local Life” experience, stop for a calamari sandwich in the nearby alleys. Your taste buds will thank you.

Recent findings suggest that after a relaxing lunch and some people watching, head to the Royal Palace of Madrid. The largest palace in Western Europe, the Baroque-style palace was built in the 18th century and is home to over 3,400 lavishly decorated rooms. It was originally built on a former 9th-century Muslim fort and today functions much like an art museum with numerous works, including pieces by Caravaggio, Juan de Flandes, and Francisco Goya. Though it’s the official residence of the royal family, they don’t actually live here anymore, and the palace is only used for official state functions. You can walk through the palace (both self-guided and guided tours are available), starting at the grand stairway, and wander through lavishly decorated staterooms. There’s also the Royal Armory, which houses a collection of medieval weapons and armor.

Recent findings suggest that to end the day, head to the Almudena Cathedral. Unlike many of the famous medieval churches in Europe, this one was constructed in the late 19th century. It was finally completed in 1993 and was consecrated by Pope John Paul II. While the exterior has a Neo-Classical design (to match the nearby palace), the cathedral also has a Neo-Romanesque crypt with over 400 columns that you can explore. Be sure to head up to the dome for stunning views out over the city.

Sources indicate that madrid is a paradise for foodies. It’s one of the reasons I keep coming back. While there are plenty of food tours to take in Madrid, I suggest heading off on your own to explore. Begin at the city’s iconic gastronomic markets. The glass-walled Mercado de San Miguel is a must for gourmet tapas near Plaza Mayor. It’s popular with the after-work crowd and is a place I usually visit a few times on my trips. Additionally, local favorites like Mercado de San Antón in Chueca and Mercado de Vallehermoso offer a deeper dive into regional flavors. Just make sure to bring an appetite.

In a recent development, if you do want to take a food tour, consider doing a food tour. This post has more of my suggestions.

For dinner, head to Sobrino de Botín, officially recognized by the Guinness World Records as the world’s oldest restaurant. It was actually a favorite of Ernest Hemingway during his time in Madrid. For a more casual vibe, go ‘tapas crawling’ through the historic streets of La Latina or Barrio de las Letras.

In a recent development, as the sun sets, head to the Gran Vía to experience Madrid’s world-class rooftop culture. Venues like The Roof at Picalagartos or RIU, 360º sky bar offer signature cocktails and dinner with breathtaking 360-degree views of the skyline.

For those who don’t eat meat, Madrid has actually evolved into one of Europe’s best veg hubs, boasting a vibrant vegetarian and vegan scene in neighborhoods like Malasaña, where plant-based versions of traditional Spanish dishes are now a staple of the city’s diverse culinary identity.

Madrid is the only European capital where nature, science, and royal history converge in a UNESCO World Heritage oasis known as the ‘Paisaje de la Luz‘ (Landscape of Light). But this prestigious area, encompassing the iconic El Retiro Park and the Paseo del Prado, is just the beginning of Spain’s monumental legacy. For more UNESCO wonders, take a day trip out of the city.

Sources indicate that one popular destination worth visiting is the Monastery of San Lorenzo de El Escorial, a sprawling imperial masterpiece recognized by UNESCO for its historical significance. El Escorial is located just one hour from the city by car and was commissioned by Philip II in the 16th century. It’s a massive palatial complex that includes a monastery, library, palace, basilica, and tomb for Spanish monarchs. Yet as massive as it is, it feels more austere than other palatial complexes, likely owing to its granite walls and symmetrical layout.

Another option for a day trip is the Royal Palace and Gardens of Aranjuez, a World Heritage Cultural Landscape that rivals the beauty of Versailles. Located just one hour south of the city, this was originally a hunting lodge, also commissioned in the 16th century by Philip II. It’s a blend of Renaissance and Baroque styles, with lavish rooms filled with tapestries, porcelain, and ornate decorations. There is lots of greenery and gardens here, which is partly why the royal family used this as their spring residence.

Industry observers note that lastly, there’s the historic university city of Alcalá de Henares, the birthplace of Spanish novelist, poet, and playwright Cervantes (he wrote Don Quixote). Just 45 minutes away by car, it also holds its own UNESCO World Heritage status, offering a perfectly preserved look into the Spanish Golden Age (1492–1659).

According to recent reports, on your last day, it’s time to get further off the beaten path. Step back into the Golden Age at the Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales and the nearby Royal Monastery of La Encarnación, two hidden palaces that house breathtaking royal art collections behind their cloistered walls.

The Monastery of Las Descalzas Reales is a convent founded in 1559 by Joanna of Austria (sister of Philip II). The name “Descalzas Reales” (which means “Royal Barefoot Ladies”) refers to the Order of Saint Clare nuns who lived here in relative austerity. What makes this monastery unique is that many aristocratic women took refuge here, often bringing their artworks and other valuables. Over the years, this turned the convent into a veritable treasure trove of art.

The Royal Monastery of La Encarnación was founded in 1611 by the wife of Philip III, Margaret of Austria. It was a royal convent, meaning it had the direct support of the monarchy. While the exterior has an austere Baroque style, the interior is quite lavish, with ornate chapels, colorful frescoes, and lots of religious sculptures and paintings. It’s also home to several notable relics, including a vial remarked to contain the blood of Saint Januarius. While tours are available, it’s still an active convent so parts are not open to the public (which, honestly, makes it all the more interesting to see).

To end your day with a local touch, head to the vast Casa de Campo park. This is the largest public park in the city, created in 1931. It covers a whopping 17 square kilometers (6.5 square miles) and includes an artificial lake, lots of paths, a zoo, and even an amusement park. Here, you can enjoy a scenic lunch or dinner at one of the lakeside terraces, offering an unrivaled view of the Royal Palace and Almudena Cathedral across the skyline. It’s the perfect place to end your trip.

While Barcelona tends to get more attention, I think Madrid is one of the best cities in Europe. It boasts a mouthwatering culinary scene, a raucous nightlife, and tons of things to see and do — no matter your interest or budget. I’ve been visiting the city for almost two decades and never get tired of the tapas, architecture, and history. The city just packs so much in and there really is something for everyone here. By following the itinerary above, you’ll see all the main sights while also getting off the beaten path in Spain’s historic capital.

Latest Update: 21 Best Places to Visit in December in the USA

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that we’ll never forget the first time we visited Fresh York City in December.
  • In a recent development, but December travel isn’t just about snow and Santa.
  • It has been revealed that in fact, we’ve been to almost all 50 states and spent a lot of winters trying to find the most fun destinations and best weather.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we’ll never forget the first time we visited Fresh York City in December. We’d seen it in movies, but standing there, seeing the Rockefeller Center tree all lit up for the first time, with skaters below and festive music in the air… it was pure magic.

In a recent development, but December travel isn’t just about snow and Santa. We’ve also spent the holidays escaping to the warmth, trading snow boots for flip-flops.

It has been revealed that in fact, we’ve been to almost all 50 states and spent a lot of winters trying to find the most fun destinations and best weather. We’ve done so many road trips in the USA and flown almost everywhere, trying to find the best places to either escape the snow or enjoy the winter, you would think we are obsessed. And we want to share all of that knowledge with you.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for the perfect winter getaway, you have a clear choice: either lean into the winter magic or escape it completely. Are you dreaming of a warm-weather escape with sunshine and sand, or a storybook Christmas town that looks like a real-life snow globe?

Based on all those experiences, we’ve put together this list of our favourite places to visit. Whether you’re looking for a festive city, a snowy mountain, or a sunny beach, we’ll help you find the perfect spot.

Here is a quick look at some of the best places for a December getaway in the USA, from festive winter wonderlands to sunny escapes.

Sources indicate that december is a month of pure magic and festive energy. It’s the perfect time to use up that last bit of vacation time for the year. The biggest draw is the distinct choice it offers: You can either dive head-first into a winter wonderland, complete with snow and holiday markets, or you can completely escape the cold weather and find yourself on a sunny beach. It’s a month of festive celebrations, incredible decorations, and finding the perfect atmosphere to end the year.

In a recent development, if you’re anything like us, sometimes the best gift in December is a break from the cold. Trust us, we know after living in Toronto, Canada. Those winters are brutal. These are our favourite spots to find sunshine and warm weather, where you can trade your winter coat for a light jacket or even a swimsuit.

It has been revealed that we love the laid-back, quirky vibe of Key West, and it’s even more special in December. We have a great memory of biking around the island, seeing the historic inns draped in holiday lights, and then ending the day at Mallory Square for the sunset celebration. It’s a perfect escape from the cold.

Why Visit in December: This is the perfect time to visit. The summer humidity is gone, the weather is sunny and warm (often in the high 70s), and the risk of hurricanes is very low. The whole island is in a festive spirit, with unique events like the “Bight Before Christmas” boat parade.

Where to Stay: We recommend finding a guesthouse or inn in the historic Old Town to be close to the action.

We once went to a holiday luau in Ka’anapali, and it’s an experience we’ll never forget. You’re eating kalua pork and sipping a mai tai, watching a beautiful hula performance… and then Santa Claus arrives on an outrigger canoe. It was the perfect, uniquely Hawaiian way to get into the festive spirit.

Recent findings suggest that why Visit in December: You get tropical weather, festive holiday luaus, and it’s the official start of the humpback whale watching season. Be aware that this is a popular time, especially around Christmas, so prices can be high and you’ll need to book in advance.

Where to Stay: Look to the resorts in Wailea or Ka’anapali for a classic Maui experience.

In a recent development, we’ll always remember snorkeling the underwater trail at Trunk Bay in St. John. The water was so calm and clear, and seeing all the colourful fish felt a world away from the snow back home. That’s the magic of a Caribbean trip in December, and the USVI makes it so easy for American travelers.

Industry observers note that why Visit in December: It’s the start of the dry season, with fantastic weather and warm, clear water. You get a full-on tropical, warm-weather Christmas experience, all without needing a passport.

Recent findings suggest that where to Stay: You can choose from large resorts in St. Thomas or more eco-friendly villas and lodges in St. John.

In a recent development, we were not prepared for how magical St. Augustine is in December. We took one of the Old Town trolley tours at night, and seeing the entire historic city, from the old Spanish architecture to the palm trees, draped in millions of white lights… it was breathtaking. It’s a holiday light display unlike any other.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: The famous “Nights of Lights” festival. The entire city is illuminated, and the mild Florida weather is perfect for walking around and enjoying the atmosphere. It’s one of the most festive and warm places you can visit.

Where to Stay: We recommend a historic inn or bed & breakfast in the downtown district to be within walking distance of all the lights.

Industry observers note that while Maui is our go-to for a resort escape, Honolulu is where you go for a vibrant, city-meets-beach holiday. We loved seeing the massive Santa surfing with his reindeer in the fountain at the Iolani Palace. The whole city has this amazing “Mele Kalikimaka” (Merry Christmas) spirit.

Industry observers note that why Visit in December: It’s the perfect blend of warm beach weather, world-class shopping, and festive displays. It’s also a significant month for history, with the memorial events at Pearl Harbor.

Where to Stay: Waikiki has a huge range of hotels, from historic beachfront properties to modern high-rises.

If your idea of a winter getaway is to truly get away from everything, the crowds, the noise, the stress, then South Padre is a perfect choice. We spent a week there, and our days consisted of long, quiet walks on the beach. It was a total reset and the perfect way to escape the winter blues.

Why Visit in December: The weather is mild, and the crowds are gone. It’s one of the warmest places in Texas and offers a simple, relaxing beach vacation without the high prices or holiday chaos of other destinations.

Where to Stay: You’ll find many beachfront condos and hotels offering great off-season rates.

Industry observers note that we thought we knew desert holiday lights, but the “Las Noches de las Luminarias” at the Desert Botanical Garden in Phoenix is on another level. Walking the garden paths lit by thousands of hand-lit luminaria bags, with musicians playing, was a top-tier holiday experience.

Why Visit in December: You get two trips in one: perfect, sunny weather for outdoor adventures like hiking during the day, and stunning, sophisticated holiday light displays at night.

Where to Stay: Choose from upscale resorts in Scottsdale or stylish hotels in downtown Phoenix.

Recent findings suggest that sometimes, the warm weather destinations just won’t cut it, especially if you are looking for that winter wonderland feel. So, this section is for travellers who want to dive head-first into the holiday spirit. These are the cities and towns that go all-out for December, with millions of lights, Christmas markets, and an atmosphere of pure magic.

It has been revealed that we’ve visited NYC many times, but there’s a specific energy in December. We grabbed hot chocolates and walked through the Bryant Park Winter Village, watching the ice skaters zip around the rink under the lights of the surrounding skyscrapers. It felt like being in the opening scene of a holiday movie. There is nothing like Upcoming York City at Christmas.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: It is the quintessential American Christmas destination. From the iconic tree to the world-famous window displays, the entire city is on a different level of festive.

Where to Stay: Midtown is convenient for seeing the main holiday sights, but we also love the West Village for its cosy, neighbourhood feel.

Sources indicate that we’d heard Leavenworth was a “Christmas Town,” but we weren’t prepared for the reality. We visited during the Village of Lights festival, and walking through the snow-covered Bavarian-style village while every single building was covered in over half a million lights… it’s not an exaggeration. It’s the closest we’ve ever felt to being inside a real-life snow globe.

Why Visit in December: The entire town transforms into a “Hallmark movie” Christmas village. It’s a full-immersion holiday experience with carolers, festive food, and incredible decorations.

It has been revealed that where to Stay: Book a Bavarian-style lodge or inn right in the village. You must book many months in advance for December.

We love Asheville, but visiting in December is all about the Biltmore Estate. We took the candlelight evening tour, and seeing the main banquet hall with its 35-foot tree, fireplaces roaring, and carolers singing… it felt like we’d stepped back in time into a Gilded Age Christmas party.

Why Visit in December: Christmas at Biltmore is one of the most iconic holiday events in the country. The city itself is a cosy mountain retreat, and the Blue Ridge Mountains are just beautiful with a dusting of snow.

Where to Stay: You can stay on the Biltmore Estate for the full experience or choose a boutique hotel downtown.

Here are the remaining destinations for the “Best Christmas Towns & Festive Cities” section, all written with unique, December-focused content.

We’ve visited a lot of Christmas markets, but visiting the one in Bethlehem, known as “Christmas City USA”, just felt right. We sipped hot cider and browsed the stalls in the old quarter, and you can feel the city’s 250+ years of Christmas tradition. The whole place is lit by the glow of a giant Moravian star on the hillside.

Why Visit in December: This is Christmas City USA. It was nicknamed this on Christmas Eve, 1741. It offers one of the most authentic and historic holiday experiences in the country, blending its Moravian heritage with a European-style Christkindlmarkt.

Where to Stay: Look for a hotel or inn in the historic downtown area to be close to the festivities.

Walking into Solvang in December felt like we’d been transported to a Danish village during its Julefest celebration. We spent the day exploring the half-timbered buildings, windmills, and bakeries, all decorated for the holidays. It’s such a unique and charming way to experience a winter getaway in the middle of California.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: The town’s month-long “Julefest” (Yule-fest) celebration is in full swing. It’s a one-of-a-kind Danish-style Christmas with parades, markets, and, of course, delicious European pastries.

Where to Stay: Choose one of the charming Danish-themed inns right in the village to be in the middle of the Julefest activities.

We had to see the “Christmas Capital of Texas” for ourselves, and it did not disappoint. The entire historic Main Street is transformed. We loved seeing the vintage railroad, which becomes the “North Pole Express” for the month. They take the “Christmas Capital” title seriously; there are over 1,400 events in 40 days.

In a recent development, why Visit in December: It is the officially designated “Christmas Capital of Texas”. The sheer number of festive events, light displays, and activities is staggering, making it a top-tier destination for families and holiday lovers.

Where to Stay: The Gaylord Texan Resort is an attraction in itself, or you can stay near the Historic Main Street to be close to the events.

A Newly introduced Orleans Christmas is an experience all its own. We did a “Reveillon Dinner,” a modern take on a Creole holiday tradition, and it was one of the most memorable meals we’ve ever had. Afterwards, we walked to Jackson Square to see the St. Louis Cathedral all lit up while carolers sang.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: You get to experience unique Creole Christmas traditions you won’t find anywhere else. The weather is mild, the food is incredible, and the city’s lobbies (like at The Roosevelt) have some of the most elegant decorations we’ve seen.

Where to Stay: We recommend a hotel in the French Quarter to be in the middle of the action and see the decorated lobbies.

Sources indicate that we went to Natchitoches (pronounced Nak-a-tish) specifically for its Christmas Festival, and it was a total joy. It’s one of the oldest and biggest in the country. The whole city, which is the oldest in Louisiana, lights up with over 300,000 lights along the Cane River, and the weekly fireworks shows are fantastic.

Why Visit in December: It hosts one of the oldest and most celebrated holiday festivals in the US, running for six weeks. It’s a classic, Southern Christmas experience in a beautiful historic district.

Where to Stay: Book a room at a historic bed & breakfast in the downtown area.

Visiting Colonial Williamsburg in December felt like walking through a living history Christmas card. We joined a candlelight tour, and seeing the historic buildings lit by real candles in the windows, with carolers in period costumes and the smell of woodsmoke in the air… it was absolutely magical.

Industry observers note that why Visit in December: You get to experience a traditional, 18th-century “Colonial Christmas”. The decorations are all-natural (no plastic lights), and the atmosphere is incredibly authentic and charming.

Where to Stay: Stay in one of the historic Colonial Houses or a tavern right in the restored area for the full immersive experience.

Here is the final category of destinations. This section is all about embracing the snow and finding that perfect winter wonderland.

It has been revealed that for many, holiday season travel is all about finding that perfect, snowy scene. These are the places to go for world-class skiing, cosy lodges, and that magical feeling of a true winter escape.

Industry observers note that we’ll always remember our first “après-ski” in Aspen. We had spent the day on the mountain hitting fresh powder whenever we got the chance, and as the sun went down, the sky lit up with this incredible pink and orange light they call “Aspenglow.” Sitting by a fire, enjoying a glass of Christmas cheer, and watching the snow fall on the historic town, it just felt like the peak of a luxury winter trip.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: It’s one of the world’s most famous upscale ski destinations, and the town is just as much an attraction as the mountains. The festive atmosphere, high-end shops, and restaurants are all decked out for the holidays.

Where to Stay: Aspen is known for its luxury hotels and ski-in/ski-out resorts.

According to recent reports, one of our favourite things about Park City is its history. We loved skiing down to the historic Main Street, popping off our skis, and walking straight into a saloon that’s been there since the silver mining days. It feels like a real Western town, not just a ski resort.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: It’s a historic mountain town with two world-class ski resorts (Park City and Deer Valley). The historic Main Street is incredibly charming, and the “Snow Globe Stroll” features life-sized snow globes you can walk through.

Where to Stay: You can find ski-in/ski-out hotels or stay at an inn on the historic Main Street.

Jackson Hole in December is just dramatic. We took a sleigh ride through the National Elk Refuge, and seeing thousands of elk gathered against the backdrop of the snow-covered Teton mountains… it was a powerful and wild winter experience we’ve never forgotten.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: It’s the perfect mix of rugged “cowboy Christmas” charm and some of the most challenging ski terrain in North America. The town square, with its famous antler arches, is beautifully lit for the holidays.

Where to Stay: Stay at a slopeside resort in Teton Village or in a hotel in the town of Jackson.

Industry observers note that we love Whitefish because it feels like a real, down-to-earth ski town. We spent a day snowshoeing in nearby Glacier National Park, enjoying the total silence and incredible snowy landscapes, and then came back to town for a casual dinner. It’s all the beauty, without the glitz. Just what we were looking for in a winter vacation.

It has been revealed that why Visit in December: It’s a laid-back, charming mountain town with a top-rated ski resort and stunning scenery. It’s also right next to Glacier National Park, which is a spectacular place to explore in the winter.

Where to Stay: You can find lodges on the mountain or stay in one of the friendly inns in downtown Whitefish.

This was a trip purely for the fun of it, and it was 100% worth it. You drive down streets named “Santa Claus Lane” and “St. Nicholas Drive,” the streetlights are shaped like candy canes, and you can visit the Santa Claus House and see his reindeer. It’s a surreal and joyful experience.

Recent findings suggest that why Visit in December: It’s the ultimate Christmas fantasy come to life. The entire town is Christmas-themed, 365 days a year, but it’s most magical in December with real snow on the ground and the added bonus of possibly seeing the Northern Lights.

Where to Stay: North Pole is very small; most visitors stay in the nearby city of Fairbanks, which has a wide range of hotels.

Industry observers note that for the best warm weather, your top choices are Southern Florida (like Key West), Hawaii (like Maui and Honolulu), and the desert Southwest (like Phoenix and Palm Springs). The U.S. Virgin Islands are also a fantastic passport-free tropical option.

Leavenworth, Washington, is often considered the ultimate “Christmas town” as it looks just like a Bavarian snow globe. Other top choices include Bethlehem, PA (known as “Christmas City USA”), Solvang, CA (for a Danish-style Julefest), and Grapevine, TX (the “Christmas Capital of Texas”).

Yes, but it depends on the park. It’s the perfect time to visit desert parks like Death Valley, Everglades, and Major Bend, where summer heat is unbearable. However, many mountain parks like Glacier, Yellowstone, and parts of Yosemite are mostly inaccessible due to heavy snow and road closures.

You are almost guaranteed to find snow in the mountain towns of the Rockies, like Aspen, CO, Park City, UT, and Jackson Hole, WY. You’ll also find snow in the Cascade Mountains (like Leavenworth, WA), Alaska, and the mountains around Lake Tahoe.

Industry observers note that december is a magical month to travel. Whether you’re chasing the sun, seeking out that perfect snowy scene, or looking for a town that’s full of holiday magic, the US has the perfect spot for you.

We hope this list, based on our own winter travels, helps you plan your next getaway. Save this on Pinterest for your holiday planning! Where is your favourite place to go in December?
